wa_cloaca_boulder.blurb: Cloaca Boulder is a cluster of blocks within Mad Meadows, the bouldering zone up Icicle Creek near Leavenworth. It holds ten problems, nearly all of them V0 or V1, with a few stiffer ones around V8 and V9 and one hard line near V11. The blocks pile together into small rooms, with huecos and a tall overhanging face, so the movement is varied and the cluster works for a mixed group: easy warm-ups for some, projects for others. The walk in follows the main Mad Meadows trail and is short.

wa_crowded_west_wall_the.blurb: The Crowded West Wall is a sport wall in the Tumblestone cluster of the Tyler Peak Crags, in the Olympic Mountains of Washington. Its ten bolted lines are on the moderate side: two at 5.7, five at 5.8 and three at 5.10. The rock is dark and blocky, and the climbs are arranged above and below a platform that you reach by following a traverse line up. It makes a reasonable stop for climbers working through easier and middle grades on short sport pitches.

wa_gully_wall.blurb: Gully Wall is the northernmost section of Last Wall in McLoughlin Canyon, near Tonasket in the Okanogan. A string of narrow faces steps up in three tiers beside a gully, with the lowest tier reached straight from the canyon floor and the others by the gully trail. Ten routes, mostly bolted with a few trad lines, run from 5.3 up to 5.9, so it suits beginners and anyone wanting easy leads. The lower tier gets morning sun and afternoon shade, while the middle and upper faces keep the sun longer into the day.
wa_gully_wall.approach: Follow the main canyon trail to the open meadow near the base of the large buttress, then cut across toward the gully where the faces begin.

wa_jy_crag.blurb: JY Crag is a roadside-accessible cliff in the Eight Mile Area above Icicle Creek near Leavenworth. The rock is golden with a glassy sheen and sharp, positive edges. Nine of its ten routes are trad and one is sport, with grades staying in a narrow band: two at 5.8, four at 5.9 and four at 5.10. That consistency makes it a fine place to build up trad leading in the middle grades. The walk up is brief, past a steep first stretch and across a meadow.
